objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (18 November 2026) on WEAVE-HEIGHTS-20261118-001's direction 1: which facing lone pairs of weave patches are bonded and how far, through the cyclic criterion; a formula or bound for the excess of bond distance over steps apart + 1 (steps + 2 from ten knots, steps + 3 from twelve) and whether it grows without limit. Found while designing: a bond's cyclic order is a geodesic polygon of weight exactly 3(m - 2), so the excess is the polygon's extra length in units of 3, and a bond search needs no state enumeration; on every disc of ten knots the excess lives only on lone pairs of opposite classes facing each other. Serves G1; tests A39 and A97.
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Successful; refereed R1, confirmed with fixes, no Block): on weave patches without holes the excess of bond distance over steps apart + 1 is the least bond polygon's extra length over the round trip (proved: bond polygons have weight exactly 3(m - 2)); to twelve knots it lives only on lone pairs of opposite classes facing each other, at most 2; the referee finds at most 2 on the facing pairs of every disc of thirteen and fourteen knots, so the maxima stop rising (0, 1, 2, 2, 2); random patches to forty knots show at most 1; whether it grows without limit is open. 5 of 5 held.
stop_rule: One frozen computation with its read-out; proof; referee hand-off; report.
title: How far the weave's rim pushes bond distance
